basis: Inherited distal motor neuron degeneration; muscle weakness and wasting reflect denervation.
Broad Xp deletion umbrella; neurodevelopmental impairment recurs across listed subtypes, but its overall frequency and other shared organ effects are uncertain.
Primary congenital glaucoma affects the eye.
Autoimmune neuropathy defined by ophthalmoplegia, ataxia and areflexia; ophthalmoplegia reflects nerve dysfunction rather than intrinsic eye damage.
Demyelinating peripheral neuropathy; wasting is neurogenic. Macular degeneration occurs in 3/14 and skin hyperextensibility in 4/14, both below 30%.
Localized amyloid deposition produces cutaneous lesions; systemic organ damage is not characteristic of this umbrella.
Cortisol excess: myopathy 80-99%; skin atrophy and immunodeficiency 30-79%. Hypertension also common, omitted under the four-axis cap; tumour origin varies.
Inherited cystic disease of the kidneys; extrarenal manifestations vary across subtypes.
Urea-cycle defect causes ammonia neurotoxicity: seizures 3/3 and coma 2/3. Reduced hepatic enzyme activity alone does not establish liver damage.
Warburg micro syndrome has defining neurodevelopmental disease, congenital ocular abnormalities and hypogonadism; genital hypoplasia supports endocrine involvement.
Dystonia and spastic paraplegia define a neurologic disorder; the mitochondrial gene alone does not establish a metabolic axis.
Tumours arise in male reproductive organs, which have no dedicated axis; endocrine dysfunction is not shared across this umbrella.
Isolated sensorineural hearing loss classified as a mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder; no other organ damage is established.
Peripheral motor nerve inflammation; the generic concept does not establish an infectious, autoimmune or other specific immune-mediated cause.
Developmental impairment, regression, epilepsy and corpus callosum hypoplasia define CNS disease.
Inherited tubulointerstitial kidney disease causes progressive renal dysfunction; hyperuricemia is variable and secondary.
Thoracolumbosacral myelomeningocele involves the spinal cord and vertebral defect; neurogenic bladder is a separately diagnosed neurologic consequence.
Defining cleft lip and palate affect the oral region; limb deficiency defects affect the skeleton.
Drug-induced peripheral nerve damage is the disease itself; the treatment exclusion does not remove its defining organ.
Defined by protrusion of spinal cord and meninges through a vertebral defect; secondary neurogenic bladder does not establish direct urinary organ disease.
Fatal neonatal hepatic steatosis is supported by the synonym and fatty liver parent; no specific metabolic defect or common extrahepatic damage is supplied.
Congenital corneal flattening, opacity and reduced visual acuity define an ocular disorder.
Primary testicular failure defines the endocrine axis; language and learning neurodevelopmental impairment affects roughly 50-80%. Skeletal fragility is variable.
Urethral and renal malformations occur in 80-99% per HPO; cortical atrophy 80-99% and intellectual disability ~60%; cardiomyopathy 80-99%. Skeletal findings lack clear impairment.
Hair and nail dysplasia affects cutaneous appendages; sparse eyelashes alone do not establish ocular disease.
